# dsh-fk-restart-button

A button at the foot of the sidebar that restarts the DSH desktop app: it closes
itself, comes back,

and the page reconnects on its own. No more closing the window
by hand and double-clicking the icon

e page reconnects on its own. No more closing the window
by hand and double-clicking the icon again.

- **Platform:** Windows desktop only.
- **Requires DSH `0.2.0-rc.2` or newer** — the version this pl

ugin was developed
and verified against, and the oldest build it is claimed to work on. The
requirem

ent is declared in `package.json` as `peerDependencies` on
`@deepseek-ai/dsh-host-webserver` (the ro

ute registration this needs) and
`@deepseek-ai/dsh-client-ui-slots` (the footer slot the button moun

ts into).
DSH checks those before importing a plugin, so an older build refuses the
install with a n

amed reason instead of mounting a button that never draws.
- **Applies to:** the packaged desktop ap

p. It refuses to run under `dsh web` in a
terminal, where killing the parent process would kill your

shell.
- **Cost of a restart:** it is a force-kill (`taskkill /T /F`), so a task that is
currently

running is interrupted. That is why the button needs two clicks — the
first arms it for 5 seconds, t

he second confirms.
- **Nothing to configure:** the plugin declares no settings namespace and has no
dependencies outside the Node standard library.
This fork adds two changes on top of upstream `dsh-restart-button`:
**1. Graceful shutdown before the relaunch**

The upstream helper force-kills with `taskkill /T /F`. A forced kill does not
give Chromium time to

flush its LevelDB buffers (`Cookies`, `shared_proto_db`),
and the 2026-10-22 incident showed why tha

t matters: the state database was
written broken and the app refused to start with `Web authenticati

on failed`,
with no config snapshot able to repair it.
The fork uses the same sequence DSH itself uses in `stop()`:
[代码示例省略，未执行]

Cost: the restart takes about 8 seconds longer. Benefit: state databases are
essentially never writt

restart takes about 8 seconds longer. Benefit: state databases are
essentially never written broken.
**2. Accumulated auth-cookie cleanup in the restart window**

DSH binds a dynamic port on every launch and mints one auth cookie whose name
is derived from it:
[代码示例省略，未执行]

A new port means a new name, old cookies are never removed, and Chromium sends
every one of them for

host `127.0.0.1`. At **71** cookies the Cookie request
header reaches 16,584 bytes, past Node's def

ault `maxHeaderSize` of 16,384; the
Host then fails with `HPE_HEADER_OVERFLOW` and the shell reports

`desktop welcome: Web authentication failed`. Measured on Node 24.21.0:
70 cookies = 16,356 B (200

These cookies hold no account data — only `authority`, `issuedAt`, `expiresAt` —
and a cookie minted

for an old port can never match a new one, so removing them
costs nothing. The login token lives in
`.credentials.yaml`.

The helper clears them in the window between the kill and the relaunch — the
[该节后续省略]
### Version requirement

The range is `^0.2.0-rc.2`, which resolves to `>=0.2.0-rc.2 <0.3.0`. DSH evaluates
it as `semver.sat

isfies(runtimeVersion, range, { includePrerelease: true })` against
the harness's own version, and r

efuses the install when it does not match. That
call was reproduced against a real `semver` for the

when it does not match. That
call was reproduced against a real `semver` for the cases that matter:
| Harness version | Installs | |

| `0.1.7-rc.2` | ❌ | below the floor |
| `0.2.0-rc.1` | ❌ | the release just before the one this was

built against |
| `0.2.0-rc.2` | ✅ | the version this plugin was developed and tested on |
| `0.2.0

-rc.3`, `0.2.0`, `0.2.1` | ✅ | later prereleases and patches of the same minor |
| `0.3.0` | ❌ | out
side the `^` upper bound, so a new minor needs a re-check |

The floor is a statement about where this was tested, not a claim about which
internal API each earl

ier build happened to lack — those builds were not available
to check. What *is* verified is the ran

ge itself: DSH's own call was reproduced
against `semver` 7.8.5, and every row above comes from runn

ing it rather than from
reading it.

A refusal is not a crash: it is one line naming the plugin, the version and the
peer that did not ma

tch, and `dsh plugin allow-version` exists to override it
deliberately.
## Why this is not a one-line IPC call

The Electron main process has `app.relaunch()`, and there is even a
`restartAppHostMenu` item — but

both sit inside a `...development ? [...] : []`
branch, so a packaged build never gets them. The Hos

t → Electron IPC channel
carries only shutdown-complete, quit-inspection and update replies; there i

s no
restart message to send. A restart therefore has to kill the whole process tree
from outside an

d start the executable again, which brings two problems this plugin
exists to solve:

1. **The helper must outlive the tree it kills.** Killing only the main process
would orphan the Hos

t and leave the server's port bound, so the new app could not
serve. `taskkill /T` takes the tree —

including any process this plugin spawned
normally, since `/T` walks the parent/child chain and a `d

etached` child is still
a child in it. The helper is therefore created through WMI
(`Win32_Process.C

reate`), which parents it to `WmiPrvSE.exe`, outside that tree.
2. **A WMI-created `powershell.exe`

does not start on this machine** — it exits
immediately with "access denied", writing no log, even f

or a three-line script,
while `cmd.exe` and `where` run from the same context. The bundled `node.exe

`
runs correctly there even with CJK in its path, so the helper is a Node script.
That also keeps th

e app's path in a UTF-8 `config.json` sidecar rather than inside
a `.ps1`/`.cmd`, which Windows Powe
rShell 5.1 decodes as ANSI.

The page recovers by comparing a per-process `token`. The gap between the click and
the kill is abou

t 1.2 s, during which the old server still answers, so "reload when
the server responds" would reloa

d straight back into the dying process. Waiting for
a *different* token can only be satisfied by a d

nto the dying process. Waiting for
a *different* token can only be satisfied by a different process.
